sunniness: The quality or state of being sunny.

subcorneous: (a) Situated under a horny part or layer. (b) Partially horny.
suprascalpular: Situated above, or on the anterior side of, the scapula.

subumbrella: The integument of the under surface of the bell, or disk-shaped body, of a jellyfish.
suite: 1. A retinue or company of attendants, as of a distinguished personage; as, the suite of an ambassador. See Suit, n., 5. 2. A connected series or succession of objects; a number of things used or clessed together; a set; as, a suite of rooms; a suite of minerals. See Suit, n., 6. Mr.

sutlership: The condition or occupation of a sutler.

succussation: 1. A trot or trotting. (old) Sir T. Browne. 2. A shaking; succussion.
subindication: The act of indicating by signs; a slight indication. "The subindication and shadowing of heavenly things." Barrow.
subnasal: Situated under the nose; as, the subnasal point, or the middle point of the inferior border of the anterior nasal aperture.

suwarrow: The giant cactus (Cereus giganteus); -- so named by the Indians of Arizona. Called also saguaro.
supraspinal: (a) Situated above the vertebral column. (b) Situated above a spine or spines; supraspinate; supraspinous.
surmullet: Any one of various species of mullets of the family Millidæ, esp. the European species (Millus surmulletus), which is highly prized as a food fish. See Mullet.
suppositive: Including or implying supposition, or hypothesis; supposed. -- Sup*pos"i*tive*ly, adv. Hammond. | A word denoting or implying supposition, as the words if, granting, provided, etc. Harris.

suprapubian: Situated above, or anterior to, the pubic bone.
subcontract: A contract under, or subordinate to, a previous contract.
supply: 1. subtriangular: Nearly, but not perfectly, triangular. Darwin.
supradecompound: More than decompound; divided many times.
subbrachiales: A division of soft-finned fishes in which the ventral fins are situated beneath the pectorial fins, or nearly so.
succulency: The quality or condition of being succulent; juiciness; as, the succulence of a peach.

supposable: Capable of being supposed, or imagined to exist; as, that is not a supposable case. -- Sup*pos"a*ble*ness, n. -- Sup*pos"a*bly, adv.
superexaltation: Elevation above the common degree. Holyday.
sucre: A silver coin of Ecuador, worth 68 cents.
sug: A kind of worm or larva. Walton.

subintestinal: Situated under, or on the ventral side of, the intestine.
subnotochordal: Situated on the ventral side of the notochord; as, the subnotochordal rod.
sugariness: The quality or state of being sugary, or sweet.
subtleness: The quality or state of being subtle; subtlety.

superimpregnation: The act of impregnating, or the state of being impregnated, in addition to a prior impregnation; superfetation.

subderivative: A word derived from a derivative, and not directly from the root; as, "friendliness" is a subderivative, being derived from "friendly", which is in turn a derivative from "friend."
subcutaneous: Situated under the skin; hypodermic. -- Sub`cu*ta"ne*ous*ly, adv. Subcutaneous operation (Surg.), an operation performed without opening that part of the skin opposite to, or over, the internal section.
subalpine: Inhabiting the somewhat high slopes and summits of mountains, but considerably below the snow line.
subdelegate: A subordinate delegate, or one with inferior powers. | To appoint to act as subdelegate, or as a subordinate; to depete.
suffragette: A woman who advocates the right to vote for women; a woman suffragist.
superpolitic: More than politic; above or exceeding policy. Milton.
suppositor: An apparatus for the introduction of suppositories into the rectum.
supinator: A muscle which produces the motion of supination.
supersalt: An acid salt. See Acid salt (a), under Salt, n.
suctorian: 1. (Zoöl.) A cartilaginous fish with a mouth adapted for suction, as the lampery. 2. (Zoöl.) One of the Suctoria.
superintendency: The act of superintending; superintendence. Boyle.
supernacular: Like supernaculum; first-rate; as, a supernacular wine. Thackeray.
superfluous: More than is wanted or is sufficient; rendered unnecessary by superabundance; unnecessary; useless; excessive; as, a superfluous price. Shak. supersaliency: The act of leaping on anything. (old) Sir T. Browne.
submetallic: Imperfectly metallic; as, a submetallic luster.
supersaturation: The operation of supersaturating, or the state of being supersaturated.
surcle: A little shoot; a twig; a sucker. (old) Sir T. Browne.
sulphuration: The act or process of combining or impregnating with sulphur or its compounds; also, the state of being so combined or impregnated.

supplely: In a supple manner; softly; pliantly; mildly. Cotgrave.
subesophageal: Situated beneath the esophagus. [Written also suboesophageal.] Subesophageal ganglion (Zoöl.), a large special ganglion situated beneath the esophagus of arthropods, annelids, and some other invertebrates.
subsensible: Deeper than the reach of the senses. "That subsensible world." Tyndall.
suffixion: The act of suffixing, or the state of being suffixed.
supersubstantial: More than substantial; spiritual. "The heavenly supersubstantial bread." Jer. Taylor.

subhyoidean: Situated or performed beneath the hyoid bone; as, subhyoidean laryngotomy.
supercilium: The eyebrow, or the region of the eyebrows.
superjacent: Situated immediately above; as, superjacent rocks.
subsphenoidal: Situated under, or on the ventral side of, the body of the sphenoid bone.
supawn: Boiled Indian meal; hasty pudding; mush. [Written also sepawn, sepon, and suppawn.] [Local, U.S.]
supercelestial: 1. Situated above the firmament, or great vault of heaven. Waterland. 2. Higher than celestial; superangelic.

supervision: The act of overseeing; inspection; superintendence; oversight.
surgeful: Abounding in surges; surgy. "Tossing the surgeful tides." Drayton.

sundown: 1. The setting of the sun; sunset. "When sundown skirts the moor." Tennyson. 2. A kind of broad-brimmed sun hat worn by women.

subriguous: Watered or wet beneath; well-watered. (old) Blount.

superb: 1. Grand; magnificent; august; stately; as, a superb edifice; a superb colonnade. 2. Rich; elegant; as, superb furniture or decorations. 3. Showy; excellent; grand; as, a superb exhibition.

sundial: An instrument to show the time of day by means of the shadow of a gnomon, or style, on a plate. Sundial shell (Zoöl.), any shell of the genus Solarium. See Solarium.
suggillation: A livid, or black and blue, mark; a blow; a bruise.
suspensory: 1. Suspended; hanging; depending. 2. Fitted or serving to suspend; suspending; as, a suspensory muscle. Ray. 3. (Anat.) Of or pertaining to a suspensorium. | That which suspends, or holds up, as a truss; specifically (Med.), a bandage or bag for supporting the scrotum.
survene: To supervene upon; to come as an addition to. (old) A suppuration that survenes lethargies. Harvey.
subpeduncular: Situated beneath the peduncle; as, the subpeduncular lobe of the cerebellum.
sublition: The act or process of laying the ground in a painting.
suspensible: Capable of being suspended; capable of being held from sinking.
supplicant: Entreating; asking submissively. Shak. -- Sup"pli*cant*ly, adv. | One who supplicates; a suppliant. The wise supplicant . . . left the event to God. Rogers.
superfluity: 1. A greater quantity than is wanted; superabundance; as, a superfluity of water; a superfluity of wealth. A quiet mediocrity is still to be preferred before a troubled superfluity. Suckling. 2. The state or quality of being superfluous; excess. "By a superfluity abominable." Chaucer. 3. Something beyond what is needed; something which serves for show or luxury. Syn.
subgenus: A subdivision of a genus, comprising one or more species which differ from other species of the genus in some important character or characters; as, the azaleas now constitute a subgenus of Rhododendron.
sup: To take into the mouth with the lips, as a liquid; to take or drink by a little at a time; to sip. There I'll sup Balm and nectar in my cup. Crashaw. | A small mouthful, as of liquor or broth; a little taken with the lips; a sip. Tom Thumb had got a little sup. Drayton.
succula: A bare axis or cylinder with staves or levers in it to turn it round, but without any drum.
sulphantimonious: Of, pertaining to, or designating, a hypothetical sulphacid of antimony (called also thioantimonious acid) analogous to sulpharsenious acid.
sumatran: Of or pertaining to Sumatra or its inhabitants. -- n. A native of Sumatra.
sulphine: Any one of a series of basic compounds which consist essentially of sulphur united with hydrocarbon radicals. In general they are oily or crystalline deliquescent substances having a peculiar odor; as, trimethyl sulphine, (CH3)3S.OH. Cf. Sulphonium.
subbrachial: Of or pertaining to the subbrachians.
subjectivist: One who holds to subjectivism; an egoist.
sural: Of or pertaining to the calf of the leg; as, the sural arteries.
subinfeudation: (a) The granting of lands by inferior lords to their dependents, to be held by themselves by feudal tenure. Craig. (b) Subordinate tenancy; undertenancy. The widow is immediate tenant to the heir, by a kind of subinfeudation, or undertenancy. Blackstone.
subordinate: 1. Placed in a lower order, class, or rank; holding a lower or inferior position. The several kinds and subordinate species of each are easily distinguished. Woodward. 2. | One who stands in order or rank below another; -- distinguished from a principal. Milton.
sunn: An East Indian leguminous plant (Crotalaria juncea) and its fiber, which is also called sunn hemp. [Written also sun.]
subpodophyllous: Situated under the podophyllous tissue of the horse's foot.
suburbed: Having a suburb or suburbs on its outer part.
superessential: Essential above others, or above the constitution of a thing. J. Ellis.
supremacy: The state of being supreme, or in the highest station of power; highest or supreme authority or power; as, the supremacy of a king or a parliament. The usurped power of the pope being destroyed, the crown was restored to its supremacy over spiritual men and causes. Blackstone.
sulkiness: The quality or state of being sulky; sullenness; moroseness; as, sulkiness of disposition.
subaid: To aid secretly; to assist in a private manner, or indirectly. Daniel.
subway: An underground way or gallery; especially, a passage under a street, in which water mains, gas mains, telegraph wires, etc., are conducted.
supperless: Having no supper; deprived of supper; as, to go supperless to bed. Beau. & Fl.
surquedry: Overweening pride; arrogance; presumption; insolence. (old) Chaucer. Then pay you the price of your surquedry. Spenser.
superstitious: 1. Of or pertaining to superstition; proceeding from, or manifesting, superstition; as, superstitious rites; superstitious observances. 2. Evincing superstition; overscrupulous and rigid in religious observances; addicted to superstition; full of idle fancies and scruples in regard to religion. Ye men of Athens, I perceive that in all things ye are too superstitious.
sustainment: The act of sustaining; maintenance; support. Milton. Lowell.
surquedrous: Having or exhibiting surquedry; arrogant; insolent. (old) Gower. James II. of Scot.
suent: Uniformly or evenly distributed or spread; even; smooth. See Suant. Thoreau.
suprasternal: Situated above, or anterior to, the sternum.
sucker: 1. One who, or that which, sucks; esp., one of the organs by which certain animals, as the octopus and remora, adhere to other bodies. 2. A suckling; a sucking animal. Beau. & Fl. 3. | To strip off the suckers or shoots from; to deprive of suckers; as, to sucker maize.
supralapsarianism: The doctrine, belief, or principles of the Supralapsarians.
surmise: 1. A thought, imagination, or conjecture, which is based upon feeble or scanty evidence; suspicion; guess; as, the surmisses of jealousy or of envy. [We] double honor gain From his surmise proved… | To imagine without certain knowledge; to infer on slight grounds; to suppose, conjecture, or suspect; to guess. It wafted nearer yet, and then she knew That what before she but surmised, was true.
survival: 1. A living or continuing longer than, or beyond the existence of, another person, thing, or event; an outliving. 2. (Arhæol. & Ethnol.) Any habit, usage, or belief, remaining from ancient times, the origin of which is often unknown, or imperfectly known. The close bearing of the doctrine of survival on the study of manners and customs. Tylor. Survival of the fittest.
suppositional: Resting on supposition; hypothetical; conjectural; supposed. South.
superlation: Exaltation of anything beyond truth or propriety. (old) B. Jonson.
sur: A prefix signifying over, above, beyond, upon.
superaltar: A raised shelf or stand on the back of an altar, on which different objects can be placed; a predella or gradino.
sustenance: 1. The act of sustaining; support; maintenance; subsistence; as, the sustenance of the body; the sustenance of life. 2. That which supports life; food; victuals; provisions; means of living; as, the city has ample sustenance. "A man of little sustenance." Chaucer. For lying is thy sustenance, thy food. Milton.
subvene: To come under, as a support or stay; to happen. A future state must needs subvene to prevent the whole edifice from falling into ruin. Bp. Warburton.
suppliant: 1. Asking earnestly and submissively; entreating; beseeching; supplicating. The rich grow suppliant, and the poor grow proud. Dryden. 2. Manifesting entreaty; expressive of supplication. | One who supplicates; a humble petitioner; one who entreats submissively. Hear thy suppliant's prayer. Dryden.
suborbital: Situated under or below the orbit.
supervene: To come as something additional or extraneous; to occur with reference or relation to something else; to happen upon or after something else; to be added; to take place; to happen. Such a mutual gravitation can never supervene to matter unless impressed by divine power. Bentley. A tyrany immediately supervened. Burke.
sulphocyanate: A salt of sulphocyanic acid; -- also called thiocyanate, and formerly inaccurately sulphocyanide. Ferric sulphocyanate (Chem.), a dark red crystalline substance usually obtained in a blood-red solution, and recognized as a test for ferric iron.
supraclavicle: A bone which usually connects the clavicle with the post- temporal in the pectorial arch of fishes.
subatom: A hypothetical component of a chemical atom, on the theory that the elements themselves are complex substances; -- called also atomicule.
sulphinate: A salt of a sulphinic acid.
sunless: Destitute or deprived of the sun or its rays; shaded; shadowed. The sunken glen whose sunless shrubs must weep. Byron.
surcoat: 1. A coat worn over the other garments; especially, the long and flowing garment of knights, worn over the armor, and frequently emblazoned with the arms of the wearer. A long surcoat of pers upon he had.. Chaucer. At night, or in the rain, He dons a surcoat which he doffs at morn. Emerson. 2.
surprising: Exciting surprise; extraordinary; of a nature to excite wonder and astonishment; as, surprising bravery; a surprising escape from danger. -- Sur*pris"ing*ly, adv. -- Sur*pris"ing*ness, n. Syn. -- Wonderful; extraordinary; unexpected; astonishing; striking.
superfetate: To conceive after a prior conception, but before the birth of the offspring. The female . . . is said to superfetate. Grew.
substituted: 1. Exchanged; put in the place of another. 2. (Chem.) Containing substitutions or replacements; having been subjected to the process of substitution, or having some of its parts replaced; as, alcohol is a substituted water; methyl amine is a substituted ammonia. Substituted executor (Law), an executor appointed to act in place of one removed or resigned.
superroyal: Larger than royal; -- said of a particular size of printing and writing paper. See the Note under Paper, n.
sulcus: A furrow; a groove; a fissure.
summons: 1. The act of summoning; a call by authority, or by the command of a superior, to appear at a place named, or to attend to some duty. Special summonses by the king. Hallam. This summons . . . | To summon. [R. or Colloq.] Swift.
suppletory: Supplying deficiencies; supplementary; as, a suppletory oath. | That which is to supply what is wanted. Invent suppletories to excuse an evil man. Jer. Taylor.
suspire: To fetch a long, deep breath; to sigh; to breathe. Shak. Fireflies that suspire In short, soft lapses of transported flame. Mrs. Browning. | A long, deep breath; a sigh. (old)
sustain: 1. To keep from falling; to bear; to uphold; to support; as, a foundation sustains the superstructure; a beast sustains a load; a rope sustains a weight. Every pillar the temple to sustain. Chaucer. | One who, or that which, upholds or sustains; a sustainer. (old) I waked again, for my sustain was the Lord. Milton.
substantial: 1. Belonging to substance; actually existing; real; as, substantial life. Milton. If this atheist would have his chance to be real and substantial agent, he is more stupid than the vulgar. Bentley. 2. Not seeming or imaginary; not illusive; real; solid; true; veritable. If happinessbe a substantial good. Denham. The substantial ornaments of virtue. L'Estrange. 3. Corporeal;
substantive: 1. Betokening or expressing existence; as, the substantive verb, that is, the verb to be. 2. Depending on itself; independent. He considered how sufficient and substantive this land was to maintain… | A noun or name; the part of speech which designates something that exists, or some object of thought, either material or immaterial; as, the words man, horse, city, goodness, excellence, are…
surrey: A four-wheeled pleasure carriage, (commonly two-seated) somewhat like a phaeton, but having a straight bottom.
substyle: A right line on which the style, or gnomon, of a dial is erected; being the common section of the face of the dial and a plane perpendicular to it passing through the style. [Written also substile.] Hutton.
surah: A soft twilled silk fabric much used for women's dresses; -- called also surah silk.
suji: Indian wheat, granulated but not pulverized; a kind of semolina. [Written also soojee.]
sulphide: A binary compound of sulphur, or one so regarded; -- formerly called sulphuret. Double sulphide (Chem.), a compound of two sulphides. -- Hydrogen sulphide. (Chem.) See under Hydrogen. -- Metallic sulphide, a binary compound of sulphur with a metal.
surfacer: A form of machine for dressing the surface of wood, metal, stone, etc.
subsalt: A basic salt. See the Note under Salt.
surpass: To go beyond in anything good or bad; to exceed; to excel. This would surpass Common revenge and interrupt his joy. Milton. Syn. -- To exceed; excel; outdo; outstrip.
subnuvolar: Under the clouds; attended or partly covered or obscured by clouds; somewhat cloudy. [R. & Poetic] Subnuvolar lights of evening sharply slant. Milnes.
subumbonal: Beneath or forward of the umbos of a bivalve shell.
subcarboniferous: Of or pertaining to the lowest division of the Carboniferous formations underlying the proper coal measures. It was a marine formation characterized in general by beds of limestone. -- n. The Subcarboniferous period or formation.
superparticular: Of or pertaining to a ratio when the excess of the greater term over the less is a unit, as the ratio of 1 to 2, or of 3 to 4. (old) Hutton.
sunstruck: Overcome by, or affected with, sunstroke; as, sun-struck soldiers.
suresby: One to be sure of, or to be relied on. (old) There is one which is suresby, as they say, to serve, if anything will serve. Bradford.
subulipalp: One of a group of carabid beetles having slender palpi.
sullage: 1. Drainage of filth; filth collected from the street or highway; sewage. (old) The streets were exceedingly large, well paved, having many vaults and conveyances under them for sullage. Evelyn. 2. That which sullies or defiles.
subimago: A stage in the development of certain insects, such as the May flies, intermediate between the pupa and imago. In this stage, the insect is able to fly, but subsequently sheds a skin before becoming mature. Called also pseudimago.
supernaturalness: The quality or state of being supernatural.
surname: 1. A name or appellation which is added to, or over and above, the baptismal or Christian name, and becomes a family name. Note: Surnames originally designated occupation, estate, place of residence,… | To name or call by an appellation added to the original name; to give a surname to. Another shall subscribe with his hand unto the Lord, and surname himself by the name of Israel. Isa. xliv. 5.
subaxillary: 1. (Anat.) Situated under the axilla, or armpit. 2. (Bot.) Placed under the axil, or angle formed by the branch of a plant with the stem, or a leaf with the branch.
superhuman: Above or beyond what is human; sometimes, divine; as, superhuman strength; superhuman wisdom.
sulphuret: A sulphide; as, a sulphuret of potassium. [Obsoles.]
suiting: Among tailors, cloth suitable for making entire suits of clothes.
sub: 1. A prefix signifying under, below, beneath, and hence often, in an inferior position or degree, in an imperfect or partial state, as in subscribe, substruct, subserve, subject, subordinate, subacid, subastringent, subgranular, suborn.
supertax: A tax in addition to the usual or normal tax; specif., in the United Kingdom, an income tax of sixpence for every pound in addition to the normal income tax of one shilling and twopence for every pound, imposed, by the Finance Act of 1909-1910 (c. 8, ss 66, 72), on the amount by which the income of any person exceeds £3,000 when his total income exceeds £5,000.
sugaring: 1. The act of covering or sweetening with sugar; also, the sugar thus used. 2. The act or process of making sugar.
sublimate: 1. To bring by heat into the state of vapor, which, on cooling, returns again to the solid state; as, to sublimate sulphur or camphor. 2. To refine and exalt; to heighten; to elevate. | A product obtained by sublimation; hence, also, a purified product so obtained. Corrosive sublimate. (Chem.) See under Corrosive.
succor: tiono run to, or run to support; hence, to help or relieve when in difficulty, want, or distress; to assist and deliver from suffering; to relieve; as, to succor a besieged city. | 1. Aid; help; assistance; esp., assistance that relieves and delivers from difficulty, want, or distress. "We beseech mercy and succor." Chaucer. My noble father . . .
substantival: Of or pertaining to a substantive; of the nature of substantive. -- Sub`stan*ti"val*ly, adv.
suroxidate: To combine with oxygen so as to form a suroxide or peroxide. (old)
superadd: To add over and above; to add to what has been added; to annex, as something extrinsic. The strength of any living creature, in those external motion, is something distinct from, and superadded unto, its natural gravity. Bp. Wilkins. The peacock laid it extremely to heart that he had not the nightingale's voice superadded to the beauty of his plumes. L'Estrange.
superciliary: 1. Of or pertaining to the eyebrows; supraorbital. 2. (Zoöl.) Having a distinct streak of color above the eyes; as, the superciliary woodpecker.
surprisal: The act of surprising, or state of being surprised; surprise. How to secure the lady from surprisal. Milton. Because death is uncertain, let us prevent its surprisal. Barrow.
sufflate: To blow up; to inflate; to inspire. T. Ward.
superreward: To reward to an excessive degree. Bacon.
supersulphurize: To impregnate or combine with an excess of sulphur.
suttle: The weight when the tare has been deducted, and tret is yet to be allowed. M | To act as sutler; to supply provisions and other articles to troops.
suppalpation: The act of enticing by soft words; enticement. (old)
succinite: (a) Amber. (b) A garnet of an amber color.
sumbul: The musky root of an Asiatic umbelliferous plant, Ferula Sumbul. It is used in medicine as a stimulant. [Written also sumbal.] -- Sum*bul"ic, a.
sustention: Sustentation. [R. or Colloq.] In fine images, in sustention, in irony, they surpass anything that Burke ever wrote. J. Morley.
supererogation: The act of supererogating; performance of more than duty or necessity requires. Works of supererogation (R. C. Ch.), those good deeds believed to have been performed by saints, or capable of being performed by men, over and above what is required for their own salvation.
supernaculum: 1. A kind of mock Latin term intended to mean, upon the nail; -- used formerly by topers. Nares. Drinking super nagulum [supernaculum], a device of drinking, new come out of France, which is, after a man hath turned up the bottom of the cup, to drop it on his nail and make a pearl with that is left;
superethical: More than ethical; above ethics. Bolingbroke.
supping: 1. The act of one who sups; the act of taking supper. 2. That which is supped; broth. (old) Holland.
subacetate: An acetate containing an excess of the basic constituent.
supramaxillary: (a) Situated over the lower jaw; as, the supramaxillary nerve. (b) Of or pertaining to the upper jaw.
subcommittee: An under committee; a part or division of a committee. Yet by their sequestrators and subcommittees abroad . . . those orders were commonly disobeyed. Milton.
subjugate: To subdue, and bring under the yoke of power or dominion; to conquer by force, and compel to submit to the government or absolute control of another; to vanquish. He subjugated a king, and called him his "vassal." Baker. Syn. -- To conquer; subdue; overcome. See Conquer.
subprior: The vicegerent of a prior; a claustral officer who assists the prior.
sunrise: 1. The first appearance of the sun above the horizon in the morning; more generally, the time of such appearance, whether in fair or cloudy weather; as, to begin work at sunrise. "The tide of sunrise swells." Keble. 2. Hence, the region where the sun rises; the east. Which were beyond Jordan toward the sunrising. Deut. iv. 47 (Rev.
supra: Over; above; before; also, beyond; besides; -- much used as a prefix.
surprise: 1. The act of coming upon, or taking, unawares; the act of seizing unexpectedly; surprisal; as, the fort was taken by surprise. 2. The state of being surprised, or taken unawares, by some act or… | 1. To come or fall suddenly and unexpectedly; to take unawares; to seize or capture by unexpected attack. Fearfulness hath surprised the hypocrites. Isa. xxxiii. 14.
suborn: 1. (Law) To procure or cause to take a false oath amounting to perjury, such oath being actually taken. Sir W. O. Russell. 2. To procure privately, or by collusion; to procure by indirect means; to incite secretly; to instigate. Thou art suborned against his honor. Shak. Those who by despair suborn their death. Dryden.
submammary: Situated under the mammæ; as, submammary inflammation.
superheat: 1. To heat too much, to overheat; as, to superheat an oven. 2. (Steam Engine) To heat, as steam, apart from contact with water, until it resembles a perfect gas. | The increase of temperature communicated to steam by superheating it.
sundry: 1. Several; divers; more than one or two; various. "Sundry wines." Chaucer. "Sundry weighty reasons." Shak. With many a sound of sundry melody. Chaucer. Sundry foes the rural realm surround. Dryden. 2. Separate; diverse. (old) Every church almost had the Bible of a sundry translation. Coleridge. All and sundry, all collectively, and each separately.
subsignation: The act of writing the name under something, as for attestation. Shelton.
subtract: To withdraw, or take away, as a part from the whole; to deduct; as, subtract 5 from 9, and the remainder is 4.
supplechapped: Having a limber tongue. "A supple-chapped flatterer." Marston.
surgery: 1. The art of healing by manual operation; that branch of medical science which treats of manual operations for the healing of diseases or injuries of the body; that branch of medical science which has for its object the cure of local injuries or diseases, as wounds or fractures, tumors, etc., whether by manual operation or by medicines and constitutional treatment. 2.
substantially: In a substantial manner; in substance; essentially. In him all his Father shone, Substantially expressed. Milton. The laws of this religion would make men, if they would truly observe them, substantially religious toward God, chastle, and temperate. Tillotson.
surround: 1. To inclose on all sides; to encompass; to environ. 2. To lie or be on all sides of; to encircle; as, a wall surrounds the city. But could instead, and ever-during dark Surrounds me. Milton. 3. | A method of hunting some animals, as the buffalo, by surrounding a herd, and driving them over a precipice, into a ravine, etc. [U.S.] Baird.
suitable: Capable of suiting; fitting; accordant; proper; becoming; agreeable; adapted; as, ornaments suitable to one's station; language suitable for the subject. -- Suit"a*ble*ness, n. -- Suit"a*bly, adv. Syn. -- Proper; fitting; becoming; accordant; agreeable; competent; correspondent; compatible; consonant; congruous; consistent.
supernatant: Swimming above; floating on the surface; as, oil supernatant on water. SUPERNATANT Su`per*na"tant, n. (Chem.) The liquid remaining after solids suspended in a liquid have been sedimented by gravity or by centrifugation. Contrasted with the solid sediment, or (in centrifugation) the pellet.
suggestion: 1. The act of suggesting; presentation of an idea. 2. That which is suggested; an intimation; an insinuation; a hint; a different proposal or mention; also, formerly, a secret incitement; temptation. Why do I yield to that suggestion Shak. 3. Charge; complaint; accusation. (old) "A false suggestion." Chaucer. 4. (Law) Information without oath;
subnect: To tie or fasten beneath; to join beneath. Pope.
susceptible: 1. Capable of admitting anything additional, or any change, affection, or influence; readily acted upon; as, a body susceptible of color or of alteration. It sheds on souls susceptible of light, The glorious dawn of our eternal day. Young. 2. Capable of impression; having nice sensibility; impressible; tender; sensitive; as, children are more susceptible than adults;
sundew: Any plant of the genus Drosera, low bog plants whose leaves are beset with pediceled glands which secrete a viscid fluid that glitters like dewdrops and attracts and detains insects. After an insect is caught, the glands curve inward like tentacles and the leaf digests it. Called also lustwort.
suspect: 1. Suspicious; inspiring distrust. (old) Suspect [was] his face, suspect his word also. Chaucer. 2. Suspected; distrusted. (old) What I can do or offer is suspect. Milton. | 1. Suspicion. (old) Chaucer. So with suspect, with fear and grief, dismayed. Fairfax. 2. One who, or that which, is suspected; an object of suspicion; -- formerly applied to persons and things;
succussive: Characterized by a shaking motion, especially an up and down movement, and not merely tremulous oscillation; as, the succussive motion in earthquakes.
subdial: Of or pertaining to the open air; being under the open sky. N. Bacon.
sudarium: The handkerchief upon which the Savior is said to have impressed his own portrait miraculously, when wiping his face with it, as he passed to the crucifixion.
subcaudal: Situated under, or on the ventral side of, the tail; as, the subcaudal, or chevron, bones.
sustained: Held up to a certain pitch, degree, or level; uniform; as, sustained pasion; a sustained style of writing; a sustained note in music.
super: 1. A prefix signifying above, over, beyond, and hence often denoting in a superior position, in excess, over and above, in addition, exceedingly; as in superimpose, supersede, supernatural, superabundance. 2.
superaddition: The act of adding something in excess or something extraneous; also, something which is added in excess or extraneously. This superaddition is nothing but fat. Arbuthnot.
superangelic: Superior to the angels in nature or rank. Milman.
surrenderee: The person to whom a surrender is made. Mozley & W.
sulphionide: A binary compound of sulphion, or one so regarded; thus, sulphuric acid, Hsulphionide.
superfuse: To pour (something) over or on something else. (old) Evelyn.
surbed: To set edgewise, as a stone; that is, to set it in a position different from that which it had in the quarry. It . . . has something of a grain parallel with the horizon, and therefore should not be surbedded. Gilbert White.
submuscular: Situated underneath a muscle or muscles.
subtegulaneous: Under the roof or eaves; within doors.
superadvenient: Coming upon; coming in addition to, or in assistance of, something. He has done bravely by the superadvenient assistance of his God. Dr. H. More.
suffix: 1. A letter, letters, syllable, or syllables added or appended to the end of a word or a root to modify the meaning; a postfix. 2. (Math.) A subscript mark, number, or letter. See Subscript, a. | To add or annex to the end, as a letter or syllable to a word; to append.
submediant: The sixth tone of the scale; the under mediant, or third below the keynote; the superdominant.
supraaxillary: Growing above the axil; inserted above the axil, as a peduncle. See Suprafoliaceous.
substratum: 1. That which is laid or spread under; that which underlies something, as a layer of earth lying under another; specifically (Agric.), the subsoil. 2. (Metaph.) The permanent subject of qualities or cause of phenomena; substance.
suspensive: Tending to suspend, or to keep in suspense; causing interruption or delay; uncertain; doubtful. "In suspensive thoughts." Beaumont. "A suspensive veto." Macaulay. The provisional and suspensive attitude. J. Morley. Suspensive condition (Scots Law), a condition precedent, or a condition without the performance of which the contract can not be completed.
sump: 1. (Metal.) A round pit of stone, lined with clay, for receiving the metal on its first fusion. Ray. 2. The cistern or reservoir made at the lowest point of a mine, from which is pumped the water which accumulates there. 3. A pond of water for salt works. Knight. 4. A puddle or dirty pool. [Prov. Eng.] Sump fuse, a fuse used in blasting under water.
supersemination: The sowing of seed over seed previously sown. (old) Abp. Bramhall.
surveillant: One who watches over another; an overseer; a spy; a supervisor.
surbase: 1. (Arch.) A cornice, or series of moldings, on the top of the base of a pedestal, podium, etc. See Illust. of Column. 2. A board or group of moldings running round a room on a level with the tops of the chair backs. Knight.
subprehensile: Somewhat prehensile; prehensile in an inferior degree.
subnormal: That part of the axis of a curved line which is intercepted between the ordinate and the normal.
subversion: The act of overturning, or the state of being overturned; entire overthrow; an overthrow from the foundation; utter ruin; destruction; as, the subversion of a government; the subversion of despotic power; the subversion of the constitution. The subversion [by a storm] of woods and timber . . . through my whole estate. Evelyn.
superstructor: One who builds a superstructure. R. North.
superstratum: A stratum, or layer, above another.
sucrate: A compound of sucrose (or of some related carbohydrate) with some base, after the analogy of a salt; as, sodium sucrate.
sublime: 1. Lifted up; high in place; exalted aloft; uplifted; lofty. Sublime on these a tower of steel is reared. Dryden. 2. Distinguished by lofty or noble traits; eminent; -- said of persons. | That which is sublime; -- with the definite article; as: (a) A grand or lofty style in speaking or writing; a style that expresses lofty conceptions. The sublime rises from the nobleness of thoughts,…
suggestivemedicine: Treatment by commands or positive statements addressed to a more or less hypnotized patient.
succubus: 1. A demon or fiend; especially, a lascivious spirit supposed to have sexual intercourse with the men by night; a succuba. Cf. Incubus. 2. (Med.) The nightmare. See Nightmare, 2.
surefooted: Not liable to stumble or fall; as, a sure-footed horse.
supervisory: Of or pertaining to supervision; as, supervisory powers.
summit: 1. The top; the highest point. Fixed on the summit of the highest mount. Shak. 2. The highest degree; the utmost elevation; the acme; as, the summit of human fame. 3. (Zoöl.) subcelestial: Being beneath the heavens; as, subcelestial glories. Barrow.

Note: Different writers name different bearings as subordinaries, but the bar, bend, sinister, pile, inescutcheon bordure, gyron, and quarter, are always considered subordinaries by those who do not class them as ordinaries.
suspectful: Apt to suspect or mistrust; full of suspicion; suspicious; as, to be suspectful of the motives of others. Milton. -- Sus*pect"ful*ness, n.
sulphostannic: Of, pertaining to, or designating, a sulphacid of tin (more exactly called metasulphostannic acid), which is obtained as a dark brown amorphous substance, H
supplyant: Supplying or aiding; auxiliary; suppletory. (old) Shak.
sunburner: A circle or cluster of gas-burners for lighting and ventilating public buildings.
suboctave: Containing one part of eight; having the ratio of one to eight. Bp. Wilkins.
succotash: Green maize and beans boiled together. The dish is borrowed from the native Indians. [Written also suckatash.]
sunbird: (a) Any one of numerous species of small brilliantly colored birds of the family Nectariniidæ, native of Africa, Southern Asia, the East Indies, and Australia. In external appearance and habits they somewhat resemble humming birds, but they are true singing birds (Oscines). (b) The sun bittern.
sunniah: One of the sect of Sunnites.
sundryman: One who deals in sundries, or a variety of articles.
surreption: 1. The act or process of getting in a surreptitious manner, or by craft or stealth. Fame by surreption got May stead us for the time, but lasteth not. B. Jonson. 2. A coming unperceived or suddenly.
subtilization: 1. The act of making subtile. 2. (Old Chem.) The operation of making so volatile as to rise in steam or vapor. 3. Refinement; subtlety; extreme attenuation.
sublunary: Situated beneath the moon; hence, of or pertaining to this world; terrestrial; earthly. All things sublunary are subject to change. Dryden. All sublunary comforts imitate the changeableness, as well as feel the influence, of the planet they are under. South.
subministration: The act of subministering. (old) Sir H. Wotton.
suf: A form of the prefix Sub-.
superfecundity: Superabundant fecundity or multiplication of the species.
subaqueous: 1. Being under water, or beneath the surface of water; adapted for use under water; submarine; as, a subaqueous helmet. 2. (Geol.) Formed in or under water; as, subaqueous deposits.
subventionize: To come to the aid of; to subsidize; to support.
surrejoinder: The answer of a plaintiff to a defendant's rejoinder.
surfeit: 1. Excess in eating and drinking. Let not Sir Surfeit sit at thy board. Piers Plowman. Now comes the sick hour that his surfeit made. Shak. 2. Fullness and oppression of the system, occasioned often… | 1. To load the stomach with food, so that sickness or uneasiness ensues; to eat to excess. They are as sick that surfeit with too much as they that starve with nothing. Shak. 2.
success: 1. Act of succeeding; succession. (old) Then all the sons of these five brethren reigned By due success. Spenser. 2. That which comes after; hence, consequence, issue, or result, of an endeavor or undertaking, whether good or bad; the outcome of effort. Men . . . that are like to do that, that is committed to them, and to report back again faithfully the success. Bacon.
superficial: 1. Of or pertaining to the superficies, or surface; lying on the surface; shallow; not deep; as, a superficial color; a superficial covering; superficial measure or contents; superficial tillage. 2. Reaching or comprehending only what is obvious or apparent; not deep or profound; shallow; -- said especially in respect to study, learning, and the like;
summist: One who sums up; one who forms an abridgment or summary. Sir E. Dering.
sulks: The condition of being sulky; a sulky mood or humor; as, to be in the sulks.
sunbeam: A beam or ray of the sun. "Evening sunbeams." Keble. Thither came Uriel, gliding through the even On a sunbeam. Milton.
succinic: Pertaining to, or derived from, amber; specif., designating a dibasic acid, C
suppute: To reckon; to compute; to suppose; to impute. (old) Drayton.
subsumable: Capable of being subsumed. J. B. Stallo.
sulphurwort: The hog's fennel. See under Fennel.
sulphophosphorous: Of, pertaining to, or designating, a hypothetical acid of phosphorus, analogous to phosphorous acid, and known in its salts.
superdominant: The sixth tone of the scale; that next above the dominant; -- called also submediant.
subjacent: 1. Lying under or below. 2. Being in a lower situation, though not directly beneath; as, hills and subjacent valleys.
suslik: A ground squirrel (Spermophilus citillus) of Europe and Asia. It has large cheek pouches. [Written also souslik.]
surcharge: 1. To overload; to overburden; to overmatch; to overcharge; as, to surcharge a beast or a ship; to surcharge a cannon. Four charged two, and two surcharged one. Spenser. | 1. An overcharge; an excessive load or burden; a load greater than can well be borne. A numerous nobility causeth poverty and inconvenience in a state, for it is surcharge of expense. Bacon. 2.
supervenient: Coming as something additional or extraneous; coming afterwards. That branch of belief was in him supervenient to Christian practice. Hammond. Divorces can be granted, a mensa et toro, only for supervenient causes. Z. Swift.
suricat: Same as Zenick. [Written also suricate, surikate.]
subsequency: The act or state of following; -- opposed to precedence.
superioress: A woman who acts as chief in a convent, abbey, or nunnery; a lady superior.
subhepatic: Situated under, or on the ventral side of, the liver; -- applied to the interlobular branches of the portal vein.
suleahfish: A coarse fish of India, used in making a breakfast relish called burtah.
surviving: Remaining alive; yet living or existing; as, surviving friends; surviving customs.
sumac: 1. (Bot.) Any plant of the genus Rhus, shrubs or small trees with usually compound leaves and clusters of small flowers. Some of the species are used in tanning, some in dyeing, and some in medicine. One, the Japanese Rhus vernicifera, yields the celebrated Japan varnish, or lacquer. 2.
suckling: 1. A young child or animal nursed at the breast. 2. A small kind of yellow clover (Trifolium filiforme) common in Southern Europe.
surge: 1. A spring; a fountain. (old) "Divers surges and springs of water." Ld. Berners. 2. A large wave or billow; a great, rolling swell of water, produced generally by a high wind. | 1. To swell; to rise hifg and roll. The surging waters like a mountain rise. Spenser. 2. (Naut.) To slip along a windlass.
supranaturalism: The state of being supernatural; belief in supernatural agency or revelation; supernaturalism.
sulciform: Having the form of a sulcus; as, sulciform markings.
susceptor: One who undertakes anything; specifically, a godfather; a sponsor; a guardian. Puller. Shipley.
surnominal: Of or pertaining to a surname or surnames.
superficiality: The quality or state of being superficial; also, that which is superficial. Sir T. Browne.
succinyl: A hypothetical radical characteristic of succinic acid and certain of its derivatives.
succision: The act of cutting down, as of trees; the act of cutting off.
suiogoths: The Scandinavian Goths. See the Note under Goths.
surtax: To impose an additional tax on.
sulphacid: An acid in which, to a greater or less extent, sulphur plays a part analogous to that of oxygen in an oxyacid; thus, thiosulphuric and sulpharsenic acids are sulphacids; -- called also sulphoacid. See the Note under Acid, n., 2.
subminister: To supply; to afford. (old) Sir M. Hale. | To be subservient; to be useful. (old) "Our passions . . . subminister to the best and worst purposes." L'EStrange.
successless: Having no success. Successless all her soft caresses prove. Pope. -- Suc*cess"less*ly, adv. -- Suc*cess"less*ness, n.
suppression: 1. The act of suppressing, or the state of being suppressed; repression; as, the suppression of a riot, insurrection, or tumult; the suppression of truth, of reports, of evidence, and the like. 2. (Med.) Complete stoppage of a natural secretion or excretion; as, suppression of urine;
surmountable: Capable of being surmounted or overcome; superable. -- Sur*mount"a*ble*ness, n.
suboperculum: The lower opercular bone in fishes.
surgeoncy: The office or employment of a surgeon, as in the naval or military service.
sulphurize: To combine or impregnate with sulphur or any of its compounds; as, to sulphurize caoutchouc in vulcanizing.
sulphury: Resembling, or partaking of the nature of, sulphur; having the qualities of sulphur.
suzerain: A superior lord, to whom fealty is due; a feudal lord; a lord paramount.
sulphurator: An apparatus for impregnating with, or exposing to the action of, sulphur; especially, an apparatus for fumigating or bleaching by means of the fumes of burning sulphur.
sudden: 1. Happening without previous notice or with very brief notice; coming unexpectedly, or without the common preparation; immediate; instant; speedy. "O sudden wo!" Chaucer. | Suddenly; unexpectedly. Herbs of every leaf that sudden flowered. Milton.
subtrahend: The sum or number to be subtracted, or taken from another.
superfecundation: Fertilization of two ova, at the same menstruation, by two different acts of coition.
succession: 1. The act of succeeding, or following after; a following of things in order of time or place, or a series of things so following; sequence; as, a succession of good crops; a succession of disasters. 2. A series of persons or things according to some established rule of precedence; as, a succession of kings, or of bishops; a succession of events in chronology.
supernatural: Being beyond, or exceeding, the power or laws of nature; miraculous. Syn. -- Preternatural. -- Supernatural, Preternatural. Preternatural signifies beside nature, and supernatural, above or beyond nature. What is very greatly aside from the ordinary course of things is preternatural; what is above or beyond the established laws of the universe is supernatural.
subpoenal: Required or done under penalty. Gauden.
superinvestiture: An outer vestment or garment. Bp. Horne.
suffer: 1. To feel, or endure, with pain, annoyance, etc.; to submit to with distress or grief; to undergo; as, to suffer pain of body, or grief of mind. 2. To endure or undergo without sinking; to support; | 1. To feel or undergo pain of body or mind; to bear what is inconvenient; as, we suffer from pain, sickness, or sorrow; we suffer with anxiety. O well for him whose will is strong! He suffers, but he…
superintendence: The act of superintending; care and oversight for the purpose of direction; supervision. Barrow. Syn. -- Inspection; oversight; care; direction; control; guidance.
suborbitar: Situated under or below the orbit.
subacromial: Situated beneath the acromial process of the scapula.
subfamily: One of the subdivisions, of more importance than genus, into which certain families are divided.
supertonic: The note next above the keynote; the second of the scale. Busby.
subsidency: The act or process of subsiding. The subdual or subsidence of the more violent passions. Bp. Warburton.
subulicornes: A division of insects having slender or subulate antennæ. The dragon flies and May flies are examples.
sumptuary: Relating to expense; regulating expense or expenditure. Bacon. Sumptuary laws or regulations, laws intended to restrain or limit the expenditure of citizens in apparel, food, furniture, etc.; laws which regulate the prices of commodities and the wages of labor; laws which forbid or restrict the use of certain articles, as of luxurious apparel.
subarration: The ancient custom of betrothing by the bestowal, on the part of the man, of marriage gifts or tokens, as money, rings, or other presents, upon the woman.
sultana: 1. The wife of a sultan; a sultaness. 2. pl. A kind of seedless raisin produced near Smyrna in Asiatic Turkey. Sultana bird (Zoöl.), the hyacinthine, or purple, gallinule. See Illust. under Gallinule.
sucket: A sweetmeat; a dainty morsel. Jer. Taylor.
surinamtoad: A species of toad native of Surinam. See Pipa.
sulphydrate: A compound, analogous to a hydrate, regarded as a salt of sulphydric acid, or as a derivative of hydrogen sulphide in which one half of the hydrogen is replaced by a base (as potassium sulphydrate, KSH), or as a hydrate in which the oxygen has been wholly or partially replaced by sulphur.
substant: Substantial; firm. "[The glacier's] substant ice." The Century.
suicidism: The quality or state of being suicidal, or self-murdering.
sunshine: 1. The light of the sun, or the place where it shines; the direct rays of the sun, the place where they fall, or the warmth and light which they give. But all sunshine, as when his beams at noon… | Sunshiny; bright. Shak. "Sunshine hours." Keble.
sufflaminate: 1. To retard the motion of, as a carriage, by preventing one or more of its wheels from revolving, either by means of a chain or otherwise. (old) 2. Hence, to stop; to impede. (old) Barrow.
surrebuter: The reply of a plaintiff to a defendant's rebutter.
supramundane: Being or situated above the world or above our system; celestial.
suscitation: The act of raising or exciting. A mere suscitation or production of a thing. South.
subcaliber: Smaller than the caliber of a firearm. [Written also subcalibre.] Subcaliber projectile, a projectile having a smaller diameter than the caliber of the arm from which it is fired, and to which it is fitted by means of a sabot. Knight.
surtout: A man's coat to be worn over his other garments; an overcoat, especially when long, and fitting closely like a body coat. Gay.
suet: The fat and fatty tissues of an animal, especially the harder fat about the kidneys and loins in beef and mutton, which, when melted and freed from the membranes, forms tallow.
sublimity: 1. The quality or state of being sublime (in any sense of the adjective). 2. That which is sublime; as, the sublimities of nature. Syn. -- Grandeur; magnificence. -- Sublimity, Grandeur. The mental state indicated by these two words is the same, namely, a mingled emotion of astonishment and awe.
superintendent: One who has the oversight and charge of some place, institution, or organization, affairs, etc., with the power of direction; as, the superintendent of an almshouse; the superintendent of public works. Syn. -- Inspector; overseer; manager; director; curator; supervisor.
surveillance: Oversight; watch; inspection; supervision. That sort of surveillance of which . . . the young have accused the old. Sir W. Scott.
subvariety: A subordinate variety, or a division of a variety.
suicidal: Partaking of, or of the nature of, the crime or suicide. -- Su"i*ci`dal*ly, adv.
sublate: To take or carry away; to remove. E. Hall.
subservient: Fitted or disposed to subserve; useful in an inferior capacity; serving to promote some end; subordinate; hence, servile, truckling. Scarce ever reading anything which he did not make subservient in one kind or other. Bp. Fell. These ranks of creatures are subservient one to another. Ray. Their temporal ambition was wholly subservient to their proselytizing spirit. Burke.
suppedaneous: Being under the feet. (old) Sir T. Browne.
suilline: Of or pertaining to a hog or the Hog family (Suidæ).
suspensibility: The quality or state of being suspensible.
supersede: 1. To come, or be placed, in the room of; to replace. 2. To displace, or set aside, and put another in place of; as, to supersede an officer. 3. To make void, inefficacious, or useless, by superior power, or by coming in the place of; to set aside; to render unnecessary; to suspend; to stay. Nothing is supposed that can supersede the known laws of natural motion. Bentley. 4.
subtractive: 1. Tending, or having power, to subtract. 2. (Math.) Having the negative sign, or sign minus.
sustentative: Adapted to sustain, strengthen, or corroborate; as, sustentative citations or quotations. Sustentative functions (Physiol.), those functions of the body which affect its material composition and thus determine its mass.
superseminate: To sow, as seed, over something previously sown. (old) That can not be done with joy, when it shall be indifferent to any man to superseminate what he please. Jer. Taylor.
substrate: To strew or lay under anything. (old) The melted glass being supported by the substrated sand. Boyle.
sucrose: A common variety of sugar found in the juices of many plants, as the sugar cane, sorghum, sugar maple, beet root, etc. It is extracted as a sweet, white crystalline substance which is valuable as a food product, and, being antiputrescent, is largely used in the preservation of fruit. Called also saccharose, cane sugar, etc.
subopercular: Situated below the operculum; pertaining to the suboperculum. -- n. The suboperculum.
subduce: 1. To withdraw; to take away. Milton. 2. To subtract by arithmetical operation; to deduct. If, out of that infinite multitude of antecedent generations, we should subduce ten. Sir M. Hale.
subvention: 1. The act of coming under. "The subvention of a cloud." Stackhouse. 2. The act of relieving, as of a burden; support; aid; assistance; help. 3. A government aid or bounty.
sustentation: 1. The act of sustaining, or the state of being sustained; preservation from falling; support; sustenance; maintenance. 2. (Physiol.) The aggregate of the functions by which a living organism is maintained in a normal condition of weight and growth. Sustentation fund (Eccl.), a fund of a religious body for support of its ministers, chapels, etc.;
submersion: 1. The act of submerging, or putting under water or other fluid, or of causing to be overflowed; the act of plunging under water, or of drowning. 2. The state of being put under water or other fluid, or of being overflowed or drowned.
subsistence: 1. Real being; existence. Not only the things had subsistence, but the very images were of some creatures existing. Stillingfleet. 2. Inherency; as, the subsistence of qualities in bodies. 3. That which furnishes support to animal life; means of support; provisions, or that which produces provisions; livelihood; as, a meager subsistence.
surfman: One who serves in a surfboat in the life-saving service.
suctorial: 1. (Zoöl.) Adapted for sucking; living by sucking; as, the humming birds are suctorial birds. 2. (Zoöl.) Capable of adhering by suction; as, the suctorial fishes.
summery: Of or pertaining to summer; like summer; as, a summery day.
superterrene: Being above ground, or above the earth.
sumless: Not to be summed up or computed; so great that the amount can not be ascertained; incalculable; inestimable. "Sumless treasure." Pope.
surrounding: 1. An encompassing. 2. pl. The things which surround or environ; external or attending circumstances or conditions.
supranaturalist: Of or pertaining to supernaturalism; supernaturalistic.
subduplicate: Expressed by the square root; -- said of ratios. Subduplicate ratio, the ratio of the square roots, or the square root of a ratio; thus, the subduplicate ratio of a to b is *a to *b, or *a/b.
sunset: 1. The descent of the sun below the horizon; also, the time when the sun sets; evening. Also used figuratively. 'T is the sunset of life gives me mystical lore. Campbell. 2. Hence, the region where the sun sets; the west.
summerfallow: To plow and work in summer, in order to prepare for wheat or other crop; to plow and let lie fallow.
subsist: 1. To be; to have existence; to inhere. And makes what happiness we justly call, Subsist not in the good of one, but all. Pope. 2. To continue; to retain a certain state. | To support with provisions; to feed; to maintain; as, to subsist one's family. He laid waste the adjacent country in order to render it more difficult for the enemy to subsist their army. Robertson.
subcrustaceous: Occurring beneath a crust or scab; as, a subcrustaceous cicatrization.
supernatation: The act of floating on the surface of a fluid. Sir T. Browne.
sutra: 1. (a) A precept; an aphorism; a brief rule. (b) A collection of such aphorisms. 2. pl. A body of Hindoo literature containing aphorisms on grammar, meter, law, and philosophy, and forming a connecting link between the Vedic and later Sanscrit literature. Balfour (Cyc. of India).
susceptibility: 1. The state or quality of being susceptible; the capability of receiving impressions, or of being affected. 2. Specifically, capacity for deep feeling or emotional excitement; sensibility, in its broadest acceptation; impressibility; sensitiveness. Magnetic susceptibility (Physics), the intensity of magnetization of a body placed in a uniform megnetic field of unit strength.
suppuration: 1. The act or process of suppurating. 2. The matter produced by suppuration; pus.
supralunary: Beyond the moon; hence, very lofty.
subcordate: Somewhat cordate; somewhat like a heart in shape.
sudoral: Of or pertaining to sweat; as, sudoral eruptions.
subpubic: Situated under, or posterior to, the pubic bones.
sulpho: A prefix (also used adjectively) designating sulphur as an ingredient in certain compounds. Cf. Thio-.
sunup: Sunrise. [Local, U.S.] Such a horse as that might get over a good deal of ground atwixt sunup and sundown. Cooper.
suppletive: Supplying deficiencies; supplementary; as, a suppletory oath.
suffrage: 1. A vote given in deciding a controverted question, or in the choice of a man for an office or trust; the formal expression of an opinion; assent; vote. I ask your voices and your suffrages. Shak. | To vote for; to elect. (old) Milton.
sumach: 1. (Bot.) Any plant of the genus Rhus, shrubs or small trees with usually compound leaves and clusters of small flowers. Some of the species are used in tanning, some in dyeing, and some in medicine. One, the Japanese Rhus vernicifera, yields the celebrated Japan varnish, or lacquer. 2.
suspensor: 1. A suspensory. 2. (Bot.) The cord which suspends the embryo; and which is attached to the radicle in the young state; the proembryo.
susurration: A whispering; a soft murmur. "Soft susurrations of the trees." Howell.
supersensitive: Excessively sensitive; morbidly sensitive. -- Su`per*sen"si*tive*ness, n.
subservience: The quality or state of being subservient; instrumental fitness or use; hence, willingness to serve another's purposes; in a derogatory sense, servility. The body wherein appears much fitness, use, and subserviency to infinite functions. Bentley. There is a regular subordination and subserviency among all the parts to beneficial ends. Cheyne.
sulphureity: The quality or state of being sulphureous. (old) B. Jonson.
surrebound: To give back echoes; to reëcho. (old) Chapman.
subside: 1. To sink or fall to the bottom; to settle, as lees. 2. To tend downward; to become lower; to descend; to sink. "Heaven's subsiding hill." Dryden. 3. To fall into a state of quiet; to cease to rage; to be calmed; to settle down; to become tranquil; to abate; as, the sea subsides; the tumults of war will subside; the fever has subsided.
subcolumnar: Having an imperfect or interrupted columnar structure.
superregal: More than regal; worthy of one greater than a king. Waterland.
subvert: 1. To overturn from the foundation; to overthrow; to ruin utterly. These are his substance, sinews, arms, and strength, With which he yoketh your rebellious necks, Razeth your cities, and subverts… | To overthrow anything from the foundation; to be subversive. They have a power given to them like that of the evil principle, to subvert and destroy.
suffossion: A digging under; an undermining. Bp. Hall.
succeeding: The act of one who, or that which, succeeds; also, that which succeeds, or follows after; consequence. Shak.
sutor: A kind of sirup made by the Indians of Arizona from the fruit of some cactaceous plant (probably the Cereus giganteus).
subalternation: The state of being subalternate; succession of turns; subordination.
suggestive: Containing a suggestion, hint, or intimation. -- Sug*gest"ive*ly, adv. -- Sug*gest"ive*ness, n.
surgeon: 1. One whose profession or occupation is to cure diseases or injuries of the body by manual operation; one whose occupation is to cure local injuries or disorders (such as wounds, dislocations, tumors, etc.), whether by manual operation, or by medication and constitutional treatment. 2.
summumbonum: The supreme or highest good, -- referring to the object of human life.
subordination: 1. The act of subordinating, placing in a lower order, or subjecting. 2. The quality or state of being subordinate or inferior to an other; inferiority of rank or dignity; subjection. Natural creature having a local subordination. Holyday. 3. Place of inferior rank. Persons who in their several subordinations would be obliged to follow the example of their superiors. Swift.
subsumption: 1. The act of subsuming, or of including under another. The first act of consciousness was a subsumption of that of which we were conscious under this notion. Sir W. Hamilton. 2. That which is subsumed, as the minor clause or premise of a syllogism. But whether you see cause to go against the rule, or the subsumption under the rule. De Quincey.
subkingdom: One of the several primary divisions of either the animal, or vegetable kingdom, as, in zoölogy, the Vertebrata, Tunicata, Mollusca, Articulata, Molluscoidea, Echinodermata, Coelentera, and the Protozoa; in botany, the Phanerogamia, and the Cryptogamia.
subsidence: The act or process of subsiding. The subdual or subsidence of the more violent passions. Bp. Warburton.
suffocate: 1. To choke or kill by stopping respiration; to stifle; to smother. Let not hemp his windpipe suffocate. Shak. 2. To destroy; to extinguish; as, to suffocate fire. | To become choked, stifled, or smothered. "A swelling discontent is apt to suffocate and strangle without passage." collier.
supraorbitar: Situated above the orbit of the eye. Supraorbital point (Anat.), the middle point of the supraorbital line, which is a line drawn across the narrowest part of the forehead, separating the face from the cranium; the ophryon.
subclavian: Situated under the clavicle, or collar bone; as, the subclavian arteries.
submarine: Being, acting, or growing, under water in the sea; as, submarine navigators; submarine plants. Submarine armor, a waterproof dress of strong material, having a helmet into which air for breathing is pumped through a tube leading from above the surface to enable a diver to remain under water. -- Submarine cable. See Telegraph cable, under Telegraph. -- Submarine mine.
suffumigate: To apply fumes or smoke to the parts of, as to the body in medicine; to fumigate in part.
supine: 1. Lying on the back, or with the face upward; -- opposed to prone. 2. Leaning backward, or inclining with exposure to the sun; sloping; inclined. If the vine On rising ground be placed, or hills… | A verbal noun; or (according to C.F.Becker), a case of the infinitive mood ending in -um and -u, that in -um being sometimes called the former supine, and that in -u the latter supine.
sutler: A person who follows an army, and sells to the troops provisions, liquors, and the like.
subsolary: Being under the sun; hence, terrestrial; earthly; mundane.
sulpharsenious: Of, pertaining to, or designating, a hypothetical sulphacid (called also thioarsenious acid) analogous to arsenious acid, and known only in its salts.
sun: 1. The luminous orb, the light of which constitutes day, and its absence night; the central body round which the earth and planets revolve, by which they are held in their orbits, and from which they… | To expose to the sun's rays; to warm or dry in the sun; as, to sun cloth; to sun grain. Then to sun thyself in open air. Dryden.
sundries: Many different or small things; sundry things.
summoner: One who summons; one who cites by authority; specifically, a petty officer formerly employed to summon persons to appear in court; an apparitor.
supererogate: To do more than duty requires; to perform works of supererogation; to atone (for a dificiency in another) by means of a surplus action or quality. The fervency of one man in prayer can not supererogate for the coldness of another. Milton.
subsume: To take up into or under, as individual under species, species under genus, or particular under universal; to place (any one cognition) under another as belonging to it; to include under something else. To subsume one proposition under another. De Quincey. A principle under which one might subsume men's most strenuous efforts after righteousness. W. Pater.
substitutionary: Of or pertaining to substitution; substitutional.
subjectist: One skilled in subjective philosophy; a subjectivist.
surroyal: One of the terminal branches or divisions of the beam of the antler of the stag or other large deer.
sulpician: One of an order of priests established in France in 1642 to educate men for the ministry. The order was introduced soon afterwards into Canada, and in 1791 into the United States. [Written also Sulpitian.]
suberin: A material found in the cell walls of cork. It is a modification of lignin.
supratemporal: Situated above the temporal bone or temporal fossa. -- n. A supratemporal bone.
sulphinide: A white or yellowish crystalline substance, C6H4.(SO2.CO).NH, produced artificially by the oxidation of a sulphamic derivative of toluene. It is the sweetest substance known, having over two hundred times the sweetening power of sugar, and is known in commerce under the name of saccharine. It has acid properties and forms salts (which are inaccurately called saccharinates). I.
supercrescent: Growing on some other growing thing. Johnson.
sullen: 1. Lonely; solitary; desolate. (old) Wyclif (Job iii. 14). 2. Gloomy; dismal; foreboding. Milton. Solemn hymns so sullen dirges change. Shak. 3. Mischievous; malignant; unpropitious. | 1. One who is solitary, or lives alone; a hermit. (old) Piers Plowman. 2. pl. Sullen feelings or manners; sulks; moroseness; as, to have the sullens. (old) Shak.
suscipient: One who takes or admits; one who receives. Jer. Taylor.
surmounter: One who, or that which, surmounts.
superscript: Superscription. (old) "I will overglance the superscript." Shak.
sulphinic: Of, pertaining to, or designating, any one of a series of acids regarded as acid ethereal salts of hyposulphurous acid; as, methyl sulphinic acid, CH3.SO.OH, a thick unstable liquid.
subdichotomy: A subordinate, or inferior, division into parts; a subdivision. Many subdichatomies of petty schisms. Milton.
sulphocarbonate: A salt of sulphocarbonic acid; a thiocarbonate.
subah: A province; a government, as of a viceroy; also, a subahdar. [India]
subtriple: Containing a third, or one part to three. Bp. Wilkins.
supravulgar: Being above the vulgar or common people. Collier.
sucking: Drawing milk from the mother or dam; hence, colloquially, young, inexperienced, as, a sucking infant; a sucking calf. I suppose you are a young barrister, sucking lawyer, or that sort of thing. Thackeray. Sucking bottle, a feeding bottle. See under Bottle. -- Sucking fish (Zoöl.), the remora. See Remora. Baird. -- Sucking pump, a suction pump. See under Suction.
supravaginal: Situated above or outside a sheath or vaginal membrane.
suspiral: 1. A breathing hole; a vent or ventiduct. 2. A spring of water passing under ground toward a cistern or conduit.
suffusion: 1. The act or process of suffusing, or state of being suffused; an overspreading. To those that have the jaundice, or like suffusion of eyes, objects appear of that color. Ray. 2. That with which a thing is suffused. 3. (Zoöl.) A blending of one color into another; the spreading of one color over another, as on the feathers of birds.
superplant: A plant growing on another, as the mistletoe; an epiphyte. (old) Bacon.
suspected: Distrusted; doubted. -- Sus*pect"ed*ly, adv. -- Sus*pect"ed*ness, n.
suspectiousness: Suspiciousness; cause for suspicion. [Obs. & R.] Ld. Berners.
surfaceloading: The weight supported per square unit of surface; the quotient obtained by dividing the gross weight, in pounds, of a fully loaded flying machine, by the total area, in square feet, of its supporting surface.
suscitability: Capability of being suscitated; excitability. (old) B. Jonson.
subalternate: 1. Succeeding by turns; successive. 2. Subordinate; subaltern; inferior. All their subalternate and several kinds. Evelyn. | A particular proposition, as opposed to a universal one. See Subaltern, 2.
sudd: A tangled mass of floating vegetal matter obstructing navigation. [Central Africa]
supercharge: To charge (a bearing) upon another bearing; as, to supercharge a rose upon a fess. | A bearing charged upon another bearing.
subincusation: A slight charge or accusation. (old) Bp. Hall.
superorder: A group intermediate in importance between an order and a subclass.
surrebut: To reply, as a plaintiff to a defendant's rebutter.
supraesophagal: Situated above, or on the dorsal side of, the esophagus; as, the supra-esophageal ganglion of Crustacea. [Written also supra- oesophagal, and supra-oesophageal.]
superinstitution: One institution upon another, as when A is instituted and admitted to a benefice upon a title, and B instituted and admitted upon the presentation of another. Bailey.
sunfish: (a) A very large oceanic plectognath fish (Mola mola, Mola rotunda, or Orthagoriscus mola) having a broad body and a truncated tail. (b) Any one of numerous species of perch-like North American fresh- water fishes of the family Centrachidæ. They have a broad, compressed body, and strong dorsal spines.
succinimide: A white crystalline nitrogenous substance, C2H4.(CO)2.NH, obtained by treating succinic anhydride with ammonia gas. It is a typical imido acid, and forms a series of salts. See Imido acid, under Imido.
supertuberation: The production of young tubers, as potatoes, from the old while still growing.
surrenderor: One who makes a surrender, as of an estate. Bouvier.
subsoil: The bed, or stratum, of earth which lies immediately beneath the surface soil. Subsoil plow, a plow having a share and standard but no moldboard. It follows in the furrow made by an ordinary plow, and loosens the soil to an additional depth without bringing it to the surface. Knight.
subsulphide: A nonacid compound consisting of one equivalent of sulphur and more than one equivalent of some other body, as a metal.
subtend: To extend under, or be opposed to; as, the line of a triangle which subtends the right angle; the chord subtends an arc.
superficiary: One to whom a right of surface occupation is granted; one who pays quitrent for a house built upon another man's ground. | 1. Of or pertaining to the superficies, or surface; superficial. 2. (Rom. Law) Situated or built on another man's land, as a house.
sumerian: Of or pertaining to the region of lower Babylonia, which was anciently called Sumer, or its inhabitants or their language. | A native of lower Babylonia, anciently called Sumer.
subereous: Of or pertaining to cork; of the nature of cork; suberose.
sulphonal: A substance employed as a hypnotic, produced by the union of mercaptan and acetone.
supervisor: 1. One who supervises; an overseer; an inspector; a superintendent; as, a supervisor of schools. 2. A spectator; a looker-on. (old) Shak.
sulphuryl: The hypothetical radical SO2; -- called also sulphon. Sulphuryl chloride, a chloride, pungent, fuming liquid, SO2.Cl2, obtained by the action of phosphorus pentachloride on sulphur trioxide. On treatment with water it decomposes into sulphuric and hydrochloric acids, and is hence called also sulphuric chloranhydride.
suffragan: Assisting; assistant; as, a suffragan bishop. | 1. An assistant. 2. (Eccl.) A bishop considered as an assistant, or as subject, to his metropolitan; an assistant bishop.
subconstellation: A subordinate constellation. Sir T. Browne.
superior: 1. More elevated in place or position; higher; upper; as, the superior limb of the sun; the superior part of an image. 2. Higher in rank or office; more exalted in dignity; as, a superior officer; | 1. One who is above, or surpasses, another in rank, station, office, age, ability, or merit; one who surpasses in what is desirable; as Addison has no superior as a writer of pure English. 2.
subscapular: Situated beneath the scapula; infrascapular; as, the subscapular muscle.
supertemporal: That which is more than temporal; that which is eternal.
supervolute: Having a plainted and convolute arrangement in the bud, as in the morning-glory.
sunbonnet: A bonnet, generally made of some thin or light fabric, projecting beyond the face, and commonly having a cape, -- worn by women as a protection against the sun.
subcarbureted: United with, or containing, carbon in less than the normal proportion. [Written also subcarburetted.] [Obsoles.]
subsign: To sign beneath; to subscribe. Camden.
succorable: Capable of being succored or assisted; admitting of relief.
supper: A meal taken at the close of the day; the evening meal. Note: Supper is much used in an obvious sense, either adjectively or as the first part of a compound; as, supper time or supper-time, supper… | To supply with supper. "Kester was suppering the horses." Mrs. Gaskell.
sure: 1. Certainly knowing and believing; confident beyond doubt; implicity trusting; unquestioning; positive. We are sure that the judgment of God is according to truth against them which commit such… | In a sure manner; safely; certainly. "Great, sure, shall be thy meed." Spenser. 'T is pleasant, sure, to see one's name in print. Byron.
subtle: 1. Sly in design; artful; cunning; insinuating; subtile; -- applied to persons; as, a subtle foe. "A subtle traitor." Shak. 2. Cunningly devised; crafty; treacherous; as, a subtle stratagem. 3. Characterized by refinement and niceness in drawing distinctions; nicely discriminating; -- said of persons; as, a subtle logician; refined; tenuous; sinuous; insinuating;
suspicable: Liable to suspicion; suspicious. (old) It is a very suspicable business. Dr. H. more.
suprasphenoidal: Situated above the sphenoidal bone; as, the suprasphenoidal appendage, or pituitary body.
sufferable: 1. Able to suffer or endure; patient. (old) "Ye must be sufferable." Chaucer. 2. That may be suffered, tolerated, or permitted; allowable; tolerable. -- Suf"fer*a*ble*ness, n. -- Suf"fer*a*bly, adv.
subjunction: 1. Act of subjoining, or state of being subjoined. 2. Something subjoined; as, a subjunction to a sentence.
subordinative: Tending to subordinate; expressing subordination; used to introduce a subordinate sentence; as, a subordinative conjunction.
subovate: Nearly in the form of an egg, or of the section of an egg, but having the inferior extremity broadest; nearly ovate.
subdepartment: A subordinate department; a bureau. See the Note under Bureau.
suretyship: The state of being surety; the obligation of a person to answer for the debt, default, or miscarriage of another. Bouvier.
supplicat: A petition; esp., a written one, with a certificate that the conditions have been complied with.
suprastapedial: Of, pertaining to, or designating, that part of the columella of the ear which projects above the connection with the stapes, as in many animals. -- n. The suprastapedial part of the columella.
succade: 1. A sweetmeat. (old) Holland. 2. pl. (Com.) Sweetmeats, or preserves in sugar, whether fruit, vegetables, or confections. Blakely. Succade gourd. (Bot.) Same as Vegetable marrow, under Vegetable.
subterrany: Subterranean. (old) Bacon. -- n. A subterranean place. (old)
succursal: Serving to aid or help; serving as a chapel of ease; tributary. Not a city was without its cathedral, surrounded by its succursal churches, its monasteries, and convents. Milman.
subdeaconry: The order or office of subdeacon.
succubous: Having the leaves so placed that the upper part of each one is covered by the base of the next higher leaf, as in hepatic mosses of the genus Plagiochila.
sublineation: A mark of a line or lines under a word in a sentence, or under another line; underlining.
subchanter: An underchanter; a precentor's deputy in a cathedral; a succentor.
supercolumniation: The putting of one order above another; also, an architectural work produced by this method; as, the putting of the Doric order in the ground story, Ionic above it, and Corinthian or Composite above this.
sublingual: (a) Situated under the tongue; as, the sublingual gland. (b) Of or pertaining to the sublingual gland; as, sublingual salvia.
supranaturalistic: Of or pertaining to supernaturalism; supernaturalistic.
sultan: A ruler, or sovereign, of a Mohammedan state; specifically, the ruler of the Turks; the Padishah, or Grand Seignior; -- officially so called. Sultan flower. (Bot.) See Sweet sultan, under Sweet.
sunk: imp. & p. p. of Sink. Sunk fence, a ditch with a retaining wall, used to divide lands without defacing a landscape; a ha-ha.
sublimation: 1. (Chem.) The act or process of subliming, or the state or result of being sublimed. 2. The act of heightening or improving; exaltation; elevation; purification. 3. That which is sublimed; the product of a purifying process. Religion is the perfection, refinement, and sublimation of morality. South.
subocular: Situated under, or on the ventral side of, the eye.
supraauricular: Situated above the ear coverts, or auriculars; -- said of certain feathers of birds. -- n. A supra-auricular feather.
subtartarean: Being or living under Tartarus; infernal. "Subtartarean powers." Pope.
subpulmonary: Situated under, or on the ventral side of, the lungs.
subarytenoid: Situated under the arytenoid cartilage of the larynx.
surfboat: A boat intended for use in heavy surf. It is built with a pronounced sheer, and with a view to resist the shock of waves and of contact with the beach.
supraglotic: Situated above the glottis; -- applied to that part of the cavity of the larynx above the true vocal cords.
supraocular: Above the eyes; -- said of certain scales of fishes and reptiles.
succeed: 1. To follow in order; to come next after; hence, to take the place of; as, the king's eldest son succeeds his father on the throne; autumn succeeds summer. As he saw him nigh succeed. Spenser. 2. | 1. To come in the place of another person, thing, or event; to come next in the usual, natural, or prescribed course of things; to follow; hence, to come next in the possession of anything;
superlunary: Being above the moon; not belonging to this world; -- opposed to sublunary. The head that turns at superlunar things. Pope.
surview: To survey; to make a survey of. (old) "To surview his ground." Spenser. | A survey. (old) Bp. Sanderson.
supersacral: Situated over, or on the dorsal side of, the sacrum.
sundog: A luminous spot occasionally seen a few degrees from the sun, supposed to be formed by the intersection of two or more halos, or in a manner similar to that of halos.
suffraginous: Of or pertaining to the hock of a beast. (old)
sulphurous: 1. Of or pertaining to sulphur. 2. (Chem.) (a) Derived from, or containing, sulphur; specifically, designating those compounds in which the element has a lower valence as contrasted with the sulphuric compounds. (b) Having the characteristic odor of sulphur dioxide, or of hydrogen sulphide, or of other sulphur compounds. Sulphurous acid. (a) Sulphur dioxide. See under Sulphur.
suppleness: The quality or state of being supple; flexibility; pliableness; pliancy.
subgeneric: Of or pertaining to a subgenus.
suscitate: To rouse; to excite; to call into life and action. (old)
suds: Water impregnated with soap, esp. when worked up into bubbles and froth. In the suds, in turmoil or difficulty. [Colloq.] Beau. & Fl.
